name: jjwt parseClaimsJwt accepts unsigned JWTs
attack_scenario: Attacker crafts a token with header {"alg":"none"} and body {"role":"admin"} and no signature; parseClaimsJwt parses it without any verification, so the server trusts the forged admin claims.
negative_test_hint: submit the unsigned token "eyJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.eyJyb2xlIjoiYWRtaW4ifQ." and assert parsing throws instead of trusting the forged admin claim

exemplar.explanation: In jjwt the one-letter difference is a total auth bypass: parseClaimsJwt and parsePlaintextJwt parse unsecured (alg=none) tokens and ignore any signing key set on the parser, so forged claims are trusted. parseClaimsJws and parseSignedClaims enforce signature verification and reject unsigned or wrongly-signed tokens.
